bullets.title: Fed turns hawkish: 9 members pencil in 2026 hikes, core PCE seen at 3.3%
bullets.body: The June FOMC dot plot showed nine members anticipating rate hikes in 2026, with six looking for two or more moves. Core PCE projection for 2026 rose materially to 3.3%, requiring ~2.7% annualized inflation in H2 to hit the median. Chair Warsh pushed back on forward guidance and leaner FOMC statements.

bullets.title: US-Iran deal shifts to execution risk; oil bears have the ball
bullets.body: Hormuz reopening could release ~93M barrels of stranded supply (54 supertankers, including ~80M barrels on 21 VLCCs ready to sail immediately), reinforcing a bearish oil outlook. Lower oil is disinflationary and supports a dovish Fed re-read; Jefferies sees a conditional rotation into consumer discretionary, airlines, housing, and autos. Execution risks remain—asymmetric deal terms, financial flows, and political cohesion.

bullets.title: Piper: S&P 500 could reach 8,450; earnings growth driving tape, not multiple expansion
bullets.body: S&P 500 NTM earnings are up 17.3% YTD; at 21.5x P/E on $393 consensus 2027 EPS, Piper models an 8,450 target. P/E expansion is limited unless rates fall sustainably, and technical setup shows waning breadth with a transition from broad bull to rotational market.

bullets.title: HF gross leverage at seasonal peak; expect pullback through late July
bullets.body: HF gross leverage posted its largest May increase on record (+22% vs 6% avg) and a sizable June increase (+18% vs 10% avg). Historically gross leverage peaks around mid-June options expiry and declines into late July/early August; decline magnitude correlates to prior increase size. HFs are net sellers in Tech, Industrials, and Materials despite those being top performers.

bullets.title: UBS upgrades MSCI AC World to 1200; favors Semis and Tech Hardware, underweights Software
bullets.body: UBS raised its MSCI AC World target to 1200 from 1120 on Middle East settlement. Regional pecking order: EM and US overweight, Europe and Japan underweight. Within tech, UBS favors Semi-Equipment, Memory, Taiwan Fabs, and parts of Mag 7 while underweighting software and online advertising. Semis are 3 std dev overbought; ML model flags Semis and Tech Hardware for near-term downside.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle intensifying: DRAM/NAND prices up 50-60% QoQ, Micron EPS upside modeled
bullets.body: DRAM and NAND prices are now tracking 50-60% QoQ gains vs. original 20-30% forecasts, with Samsung 2Q26 operating profit expected to exceed W100tr. Citi models 6% EPS upside for Micron's May quarter with $28+ Aug-Q EPS on 20%+ DRAM ASPs YoY. Micron reports June 24 alongside QCOM Investor Day; consensus EPS $20.57, revenue $35.56B.

bullets.title: Backend AI switch market exploding: Ethernet +100% YoY to $3.7B, InfiniBand +200% YoY to $2B
bullets.body: 800G Ethernet dominates ~80% of revenue and ~70% of ports. 1.6T remains below 1% but is expected to ramp in 2H with Amazon and Google first, Meta in 1H27 via CPO. CLS holds #1 share at >25% (down ~5pts YoY), NVDA at 24% (down 6pts), CSCO surging +8pts to ~8% overall and ~13% within top-4 cloud customers on Meta deployments, ANET gaining modestly to 12%.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI cost crunch: Uber burned full 2026 AI budget in 4 months; Walmart and Microsoft also capping usage
bullets.body: Enterprise AI adoption is stalling not on capability but on cost, governance, and compliance. Median AI spend is $11.38/month per employee, but top 1% spend ~$7,500/month; software engineers run ~$730/month in token costs. Pricing is shifting to usage-based models, and data privacy remains the biggest adoption obstacle.

bullets.title: AWS agentic AI scaling: Citi projects +37% YoY FY27 revenue growth; Bedrock AgentCore up 15x in 6 months
bullets.body: Citi's AWS NYC Summit takeaway is bullish on Amazon: Bedrock AgentCore agent task volume up 15x in six months, with new products spanning agentic context, security, and DevOps. FY27 AWS growth projected at +37% YoY vs +30% in FY26. Positive read-through for data infrastructure names ORCL, SNOW, MDB, MSFT, and ESTC.

bullets.title: AI observability/resiliency emerging as must-have prereq for enterprise AI productionization
bullets.body: AWS Summit field checks show enterprises lack oversight and control of AI agent activity, creating visibility and security bottlenecks blocking full-scale AI production. Budgets remain resilient for observability modernization and resiliency tools, with strong booth traffic and conversation share for platforms displacing legacy vendors.

bullets.title: Accenture hits 2017 lows: weak bookings, macro disruption, large deals slipping to FY27
bullets.body: ACN F3Q revenue of $18.72B slightly missed; geopolitical disruption cost ~$100M in consulting revenue and ~$400M in bookings, with large managed services deals ($300-500M) slipping to FY27. FY26 FXN growth guidance narrowed to +3-4%. JPMorgan maintains Overweight but cuts PT to $179 from $201, noting ACN's M&A expansion ($5B to $9B target in FY26) and strong EPS protection ($3.80 vs $3.64 consensus).

bullets.title: ASML EUV: geopolitical China headlines likely noise; 90-tool guidance may be a floor
bullets.body: ASML confirmed no EUV shipments to China; Bloomberg report of an EUV reaching China is seen as unlikely given the tools' physical complexity (bus-sized, 180 tons). GS notes the 90-tool EUV guidance may have upside to 110-120 units via Terafab discussions. JPMorgan separately raises FY26/27 operating profit for Tokyo Electron above consensus on +28-29% WFE growth.

bullets.title: China AI margin squeeze: API pricing flat/down while hardware costs surge; US widening capability gap
bullets.body: US AI API pricing is up 89% March-to-June with Anthropic models now ranked #1 globally, widening the US-China capability gap from 8% to 13%. Chinese labs face the opposite dynamic: flat or declining API pricing (MiniMax cut -33%) while hardware costs (memory, Huawei chips) rise sharply. China AI labs face acute profitability pressure amid compute shortages.

bullets.title: SaaS indexes down 15.7% YTD vs S&P +10.1%; agent wave seen benefiting NOW, TEAM, CRM
bullets.body: Wolfe sees SNOW and MDB as public proxies for Databricks-like AI/data trends (Databricks core ARR +65%), with enterprise agent wave benefiting NOW, TEAM, and CRM. All-SaaS index trades at 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales. PLTR seen as best product-market fit but valuation warrants caution.

bullets.title: EM fund outflows decelerating; Taiwan and Korea turning positive
bullets.body: EM equity outflows eased to -$1.8bn from -$2.8bn the prior week and -$7.5bn two weeks prior. Taiwan recovered with +$2.2bn inflows after record -$13.9bn outflows; Korea turned positive at +$799mn after five consecutive weeks of heavy selling (~$47bn cumulative). India saw small +$323mn inflows after seven weeks of outflows. YTD EM equity flows remain positive at +$56.9bn.

bullets.title: ESG ETF inflows surged 218% last week to $2.14B; ninth straight week of net inflows
bullets.body: ESG ETF net inflows expanded 218% week-over-week to $2.14B, marking the ninth consecutive week of positive flows. Green economy companies are now valued at a record $10 trillion market cap with $5.5 trillion in climate-solution revenue.

bullets.title: Fed proposes stablecoin tracking framework; power/grid legislation advancing for AI data centers
bullets.body: The Fed proposed an identification framework to monitor stablecoin issuers within the payment ecosystem. Separately, Microsoft-backed bipartisan legislation would require large power users to fund grid upgrades for data centers, and FERC approved a Trump administration plan to speed AI data centers' grid connectivity.

bullets.title: UK political transition: Burnham likely PM by September; corporation tax hike most probable fiscal shift
bullets.body: Andy Burnham won the Makerfield by-election with 55% and a 9,000+ margin, giving him strong momentum to become Prime Minister by Labour's September conference. JPMorgan sees high risk he changes fiscal rules and targets corporation tax as the most likely rate increase, with a potential active November Budget.
